title: H4K20me3 and CTCF act reciprocally at TAD boundaries to regulate cell state transitions
authors: Atai, K., Mitra, M., Bohn, E. et al.
abstract: Reversible transitions between proliferative and quiescent cell states involve widespread gene expression changes despite stable topologically associating domain (TAD) positioning. We report a reciprocal antagonism between TAD boundary element CTCF and histone modification H4K20me3 as a central mechanism governing the proliferation-quiescence transition.
